From Where to Where: Straight across the widest part of the forehead. Placement zone by guide: halfway between the hairline and the eyebrows (thefacereport.com; glowprint.app; faceshapedetector.app blog); about one finger above the eyebrows taken hairline edge to hairline edge (oblongfaceshape.com); about a finger-width below the hairline (glowtira.app)
How to Take It: Soft tape or string kept level across the face. To locate a hidden hairline the webflow PDF guide gives its palm trick: lay the palm across the brows with the little finger on the eyebrows and the index-finger knuckle marks the hairline; it then slides a finger up from the outer end of the brow to about half its height to place the side edges
Warnings the Guides State: Use soft tape or string not a rigid ruler (webflow PDF guide; faceshapedetector.app how-to page); hair fully tied back before measuring (every guide in the set)

From Where to Where: Straight across the outermost cheekbone points. The guides place it just below the outer corners of the eyes (thefacereport.com; glowprint.app; oblongfaceshape.com; faceshapedetector.app)
How to Take It: The webflow PDF guide locates the bone by running a finger straight down from the outer eye corner until it hits bone; then measure level across both points
Warnings the Guides State: faceshapedetector.app states the most common measurement error is taking cheekbone width too low - reading the fleshy cheeks instead of the bone

From Where to Where: Method A corner-to-corner: straight across the widest part of the jaw corner to corner without following the curve down to the chin (oblongfaceshape.com); from one jaw angle where the jaw turns up toward the ear across to the other (thefacereport.com); from the angle of the jaw on one side across to the other passing under the chin (glowprint.app); from one jaw corner to the other across the bottom of the face (faceshapedetector.app main guide). Method B chin-to-angle doubled: from below the ear down to the tip of the chin multiplied by two (webflow PDF guide); from the middle of the chin up to where the jaw naturally curves doubled (faceshapedetector.app blog)
How to Take It: Pick one method knowingly and note which one you used because the J number changes with the method and so does every threshold that touches it. On placement: the jaw angle sits about 2-3 cm above the chin point on most people (faceshapedetector.app main guide)
Warnings the Guides State: oblongfaceshape.com names the chin-to-ear reading a common mistake; the webflow PDF guide warns that starting below the ear has produced abnormally large jawline measurements; oblongfaceshape.com notes a clenched jaw reads wider by several millimetres; the doubling method assumes both sides match while corner-to-corner does not

From Where to Where: From the centre of the hairline straight down to the tip of the chin (every guide in the set). With a widow's peak measure from the peak itself not the surrounding hairline (webflow PDF guide)
How to Take It: Take each reading twice and average the pair (faceshapedetector.app blog)
Warnings the Guides State: faceratio.netlify.app states its analyzer measures from the top of the detected outline (mid-forehead) so a tape from the hairline typically reads about 0.15-0.25 higher and its thresholds are calibrated to the analyzer; thefacereport.com states its photo detector cannot see the true hairline so the two ratio numbers will not be identical; glowtira.app notes a high ponytail adds 2-4 cm of perceived length; faceshapedetector.app blog states 1 cm of positioning error can flip a shape
